sources.cite: Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission Act compilation (A.C.A. Tit. 23, Subt. 4, Ch. 112)
sources.version: Commission-hosted copy of the Arkansas Code of 1987 Annotated Official Edition, 'CURRENT THROUGH THE 2011 REGULAR SESSION AND UPDATES ... THROUGH JUNE 2, 2011'. Used to confirm the pre-2015 text of § 313(e).

also.treatment: Recall campaign work is inside § 313 itself ('warranty or recall campaign agreements', (a); (c)(1)-(3)), so the (e) claim, audit and chargeback rules apply directly. Recall-remedy and stop-sale reimbursement claims under § 319 are expressly 'subject to the same limitations and requirements as a warranty reimbursement claim made under § 23-112-313', and § 319(c) bars reducing compensation (chargeback, incentive removal or reduction) because a dealer filed a § 319 claim unless the reduction is applied uniformly statewide.

The audit and charge-back provisions of § 313(e) 'also apply to all other incentive and reimbursement programs', but the window is 12 months after 'the date of the transactions', not the payment/credit date used for warranty claims. The 90-day Commission appeal and the stay apply ('any chargeback under this subdivision (e)(4)').

Not named. A manufacturer-funded maintenance or service-contract reimbursement program would fall under 'all other incentive and reimbursement programs' on a plain reading ((e)(4)(B)); 'routine maintenance' is defined in (f) only to exclude it from the retail-rate calculation.
Not named; same reasoning as maintenance: a manufacturer reimbursement program is reached by (e)(4)(B) with the 12-month transaction-date window.

Separate regime in § 310(d)(1)(D): 45-day decision or deemed approval; if submitted ROs show a rate substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the manufacturer may request additional documentation for 45 days before or after the submitted period. No frequency limit and no audit-triggered rate consequence.

covers_line: Factory warranty and recall claims; recall-remedy and stop-sale claims under § 23-112-319 (same limits); incentive and reimbursement programs (12 months from the transaction date).

rules.label: Audit window
rules.short: One year from the date the claim was paid or credit issued (warranty and recall claims).
rules.value: Warranty and recall claims: within a one-year period from the date the claim was paid or credit was issued by the manufacturer or franchiser. The year is stated as the period for the audit; no separate date is given for levying the resulting chargeback (see recovery_deadline).
rules.quote: Audit the claims within a one-year period from the date the claim was paid or credit issued by the manufacturer or franchiser

rules.label: Window trigger for incentive and reimbursement programs
rules.short: Incentive and other reimbursement programs: 12 months from the date of the transactions, not from payment.
rules.value: Incentive and all other reimbursement programs: the audit and charge-back provisions apply for 12 months after the date of the transactions subject to audit. The trigger is the transaction date, not the date the manufacturer paid or credited the dealer (which is the trigger for warranty and recall claims).
rules.quote: The audit and charge-back provisions of this subsection also apply to all other incentive and reimbursement programs for a period of twelve (12) months after the date of the transactions that are subject to audit by the franchiser.

rules.label: Post-window exception (fraud)
rules.short: Fraud only: a chargeback is allowed if the manufacturer establishes fraud in an Arkansas court, within two years of the claim date. Whether the two years bounds the court finding or the chargeback is not stated.
rules.value: Fraud only. The manufacturer may charge back a fraudulent claim if it establishes in a court of competent jurisdiction in Arkansas that the claim is fraudulent, within a period not to exceed two years from the date of the claim. There is no extension for intentional misrepresentation, lack of cooperation or similar. Conservative reading: obtain the court finding AND take the chargeback within two years of the claim date.
rules.reason: The court-finding prerequisite and the two-year outer limit are express, but the sentence does not say whether 'within a period not to exceed two (2) years' governs the court finding or the chargeback. (e)(4)(C) also names only 'the manufacturer' where (e)(4)(A) names 'the manufacturer or franchiser' (see fraud_carveout_actor).
rules.quote: charge back any fraudulent claim if the manufacturer establishes in a court of competent jurisdiction in this state that the claim is fraudulent within a period not to exceed two (2) years from the date of the claim

rules.label: Deadline to take the chargeback
rules.short: Not stated; the year is written as the audit period, and a pending Commission appeal can push the levy past it. Conservative: audit and notify within the year.
rules.value: Not stated. The one-year period in (e)(4)(A)(ii) is written as the period within which to 'Audit the claims'; the chargeback right in (iii) carries no deadline; and (e)(4)(D)(ii) bars levying while a Commission appeal is pending, which can push an actual levy past the year. Conservative practice: finish the audit and give the chargeback notification within one year of payment or credit.
rules.reason: The audit window and the chargeback right sit in separate clauses, and nothing says whether a chargeback arising from a timely audit may be notified or levied after the one-year (or 12-month) period ends.
rules.note: No single sentence states a chargeback deadline; the relevant words are the (e)(4)(A)(ii) audit-window quote above and (e)(4)(A)(iii) 'Charge back any false or unsubstantiated claims.'

rules.label: Grounds to charge back a paid claim
rules.short: Only 'false or unsubstantiated' claims. 'Unsubstantiated' isn't defined; read with the documentation right, a paid claim the dealer can't support is the natural case.
rules.value: Only 'false or unsubstantiated' claims may be charged back. 'Unsubstantiated' is not defined; read with (e)(4)(A)(i) (manufacturer may require documentation), a paid claim the dealer cannot support with the required documentation is the natural case. Fraudulent claims outside the one-year window go through the separate court-finding route in (e)(4)(C). The denial-side rules (clerical error, work properly performed) are not cross-referenced into this ground.
rules.quote: Charge back any false or unsubstantiated claims.
rules.pinpoint: Ark. Code Ann. § 23-112-313(e)(4)(A)(iii); (e)(4)(B) for incentive and reimbursement programs

rules.label: Grounds to deny an unpaid claim
rules.short: No list. Pay for warranty work properly performed per the manufacturer's requirements; no disapproval for a clerical error that doesn't change the amount; written disapproval with specific grounds within 30 days or deemed approved.
rules.value: No list of denial grounds. Three limits apply to an unpaid claim: (1) the manufacturer shall pay for warranty work properly performed in accordance with its requirements (§ 310(d)(3)); (2) a claim shall not be disapproved for a clerical error that does not render the amount incorrect (§ 313(e)(3)(A)); (3) a disapproval must be in writing within 30 days of submission and state the specific grounds (§ 313(e)(2)(A)(i); § 310(d)(2)(B)). These are denial rules; the statute does not carry them into the chargeback ground, which is only 'false or unsubstantiated'.
rules.quote: shall pay a motor vehicle dealer for warranty work, as long as the work in question was properly performed in accordance with requirements of the manufacturer

rules.label: Proof and documentation
rules.short: The manufacturer may require documentation for claims (no stated limit); no standard of proof for 'false or unsubstantiated'; fraud must be established in court.
rules.value: The manufacturer or franchiser may require documentation for claims; no limit on what may be required is stated. No standard of proof is stated for finding a paid claim 'false or unsubstantiated'. The only stated evidentiary burden is for fraud: it must be established in an Arkansas court of competent jurisdiction before a fraud chargeback.

rules.label: Clerical error (disapproval rule)
rules.short: No DISAPPROVAL for a clerical error that doesn't change the amount (including prior-approval errors). Whether such a paid claim can later be charged back as 'unsubstantiated' is unresolved.
rules.value: A claim shall not be DISAPPROVED because of a clerical error that does not render the claim amount incorrect, including clerical errors arising from the manufacturer's or distributor's prior-approval process. Act 1055 of 2015 removed the former 'provided the dealer receives preapproval' condition. The rule governs disapproval of a submitted claim; it does not say whether such a claim, once paid, may be charged back as 'unsubstantiated' (see legal review).
rules.quote: A claim shall not be disapproved because a clerical error was made that does not render the amount of the claim incorrect, including without limitation clerical errors that occur as a result of a manufacturer or distributor's prior approval process.

rules.label: Written reasons
rules.short: Required for disapprovals (specific grounds within 30 days). For chargebacks the statute says only 'notification', which starts the dealer's 90-day appeal clock: give dated written notice with reasons.
rules.value: Disapproval of a submitted claim: written notice within the 30-day decision period stating the specific grounds. Chargebacks: the statute refers only to 'notification by the manufacturer or distributor', which starts the dealer's 90-day Commission appeal clock; no form or content is prescribed. Practice: give dated written chargeback notice with reasons, since the appeal window runs from notification.
rules.quote: The motor vehicle dealer who submits a claim which is disapproved shall be notified in writing of the disapproval within the same period, and the notice shall state the specific grounds upon which the disapproval is based.

rules.label: Cure and resubmission
rules.short: Disapproved unpaid claims: correct and resubmit within 30 days. No cure right after a chargeback; the dealer's route is the Commission appeal.
rules.value: Disapproved (unpaid) claims only: the dealer may correct and resubmit within 30 days of receipt of the disapproval, and resubmitted claims get the same 30-day decision clock ((e)(1): 'either original or resubmitted'). No cure, correction or resubmission right is stated after a chargeback of a paid claim; the dealer's remedy there is the Commission appeal.
rules.quote: The motor vehicle dealer may correct and resubmit the disapproved claims within thirty (30) days of receipt of disapproval.

rules.label: Manufacturer internal appeal
rules.short: Not required; the statute assumes one may exist for disapprovals.
rules.value: Not required. The statute says a dealer 'may contest the disapproval through the manufacturer's appeals process' but imposes no duty to maintain one, and the sentence follows the clerical-error disapproval rule. Nothing addresses an internal appeal of a chargeback; the statutory route for chargebacks is the Commission appeal.
rules.reason: (e)(3)(B) assumes an appeals process exists and lets the dealer use it for a disapproval; it contains no 'shall maintain' language and does not mention chargebacks.
rules.quote: However, a dealer may contest the disapproval through the manufacturer's appeals process.

rules.label: Stay while the Commission appeal is pending
rules.short: Once the dealer appeals to the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission, the chargeback may not be levied until the appeal is resolved; hearing within 120 days unless the parties agree to settle.
rules.value: Once the dealer files an appeal of the chargeback with the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission, the manufacturer or distributor shall not levy the chargeback until the appeal is resolved. The Commission must hold a hearing within 120 days of filing unless all parties have agreed to settle. Applies to 'any chargeback under this subdivision (e)(4)', so warranty, recall and incentive/reimbursement-program chargebacks alike.
rules.quote: If a dealer files an appeal of the chargeback with the commission, the manufacturer or distributor shall not levy the chargeback until the appeal is resolved.

rules.label: Minimum wait after chargeback notice
rules.short: No minimum wait stated. The dealer has 90 days from notification to appeal; conservative practice is to hold the levy until that window closes or the appeal is resolved.
rules.value: No minimum wait is stated. The dealer has 90 days from notification to appeal, and once an appeal is filed the chargeback 'shall not' be levied until the appeal is resolved. The text does not say whether a chargeback levied inside the 90-day window must be reversed when an appeal is then filed. Conservative practice: do not levy until the 90-day window closes without an appeal, or the appeal is resolved.
rules.reason: (e)(4)(D)(ii) bars levying after an appeal is filed; (D)(i) gives the dealer 90 days to file; nothing addresses a levy made before an appeal is filed.
rules.quote: A dealer may file an appeal with the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission to protest any chargeback under this subdivision (e)(4) within ninety (90) days of notification by the manufacturer or distributor.

rules.label: Recall-remedy and stop-sale reimbursement claims take the § 313 limits
rules.short: Recall-remedy and stop-sale reimbursement claims under § 23-112-319 take the same audit window, grounds, fraud route, appeal and stay.
rules.value: A dealer's reimbursement claim for a recall remedy or repair, or for stop-sale/do-not-drive compensation on a used vehicle when no part or remedy is reasonably available, is subject to the same limitations and requirements as a warranty reimbursement claim under § 313 (unless paid under a national recall compensation program that pays at least as much, or as otherwise agreed). So the one-year audit window, 'false or unsubstantiated' ground, fraud route, 90-day appeal and stay apply to those claims.
rules.quote: Is subject to the same limitations and requirements as a warranty reimbursement claim made under § 23-112-313

rules.label: No chargeback or incentive reduction because a § 319 recall claim was filed
rules.short: No chargeback, incentive removal or incentive reduction because a dealer filed a § 319 recall claim, unless applied uniformly to all same-line dealers in the state.
rules.value: It is a violation for a manufacturer to reduce compensation otherwise owed to a dealer because the dealer submitted a § 319 reimbursement claim, including through a chargeback, removal from an incentive program, or a reduction in the amount owed under an incentive program. Exception: a reduction applied uniformly to all new motor vehicle dealers of the same line make in the state. § 319 reaches used vehicles under a federal safety or emissions recall with a stop-sale or do-not-drive order and parts unavailable 30 days or longer.
rules.quote: It is a violation of this section for a manufacturer to reduce the amount of compensation otherwise owed to a new motor vehicle dealer because the new motor vehicle dealer has submitted a claim for reimbursement under this section

rules.label: Fraud carve-out is written for 'the manufacturer' only
rules.short: The fraud carve-out names only 'the manufacturer'; the audit right names 'the manufacturer or franchiser'. A distributor acting as franchiser needs legal review before using the two-year fraud route.
rules.value: (e)(4)(A) gives audit and chargeback rights to 'the manufacturer or franchiser' and (e)(4)(D) refers to 'the manufacturer or distributor', but the fraud carve-out in (e)(4)(C) says 'the manufacturer retains the right'. § 23-112-103(14) treats a distributor as a 'franchiser'. A distributor that is the franchiser should not assume it can use the two-year fraud route without legal review.
rules.reason: The three clauses of (e)(4) name different actors; nothing in § 313 or the § 103 definitions says whether 'manufacturer' in (C) includes a distributor-franchiser.
rules.quote: However, the manufacturer retains the right to charge back any fraudulent claim

rules.label: Rate-submission validation: 45-day documentation window
rules.value: Rate-change requests: approve or disapprove within 45 days of receipt or the request is approved. If the submitted repair orders show a labor rate or parts markup substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the manufacturer or distributor may request additional documentation for 45 days before or 45 days after the submitted period. That is the only validation step the statute names. The dealer's ROs must come from the lesser of 100 sequential customer-pay ROs or a 90-day look-back, with repair dates within 180 days before submission (§ 313(c)(6)(B)). No frequency limit on requests; no audit-triggered rate consequence.
rules.quote: may request additional documentation for a period of either forty-five (45) days prior or forty-five (45) days subsequent to the time period for which the repair orders were submitted

rules.label: Deemed approval and payment clock
rules.value: Claims not specifically disapproved in writing within 30 days of submission are deemed approved and must be paid within 30 days; approved claims are paid within 30 days following approval (§ 310(d)(2)(A)). The statute does not exempt deemed-approved claims from the one-year audit. Note the codified (e)(1) reads 'within thirty (30) days following their approval or disapproval' (a drafting defect carried since Act 756 of 2009); the operative 30-day clocks are in (e)(2)(B) and § 310(d)(2)(B).
rules.quote: Any claims not specifically disapproved in writing within thirty (30) days from their submission shall be deemed approved, and payment shall follow within thirty (30) days.

rules.label: Over-the-air / remote update assistance is compensable
rules.value: Added by Act 515 of 2023: the manufacturer, distributor or branch shall compensate a dealer that provides customer-requested assistance with an over-the-air or remote change, repair or update performed at the dealer's location or other manufacturer-authorized repair location. Expect these as a claim category under § 313; the statute sets no separate audit or chargeback rule for them.
rules.quote: shall compensate a motor vehicle dealer that provides assistance requested by a customer whose motor vehicle was subjected to an over-the-air or remote change, repair, or update

not_addressed.label: Audit frequency cap
not_addressed.note: The only 'reasonable basis' language for warranty audits is in the Recreational Vehicle Franchise Act (§ 23-112-1016(b)(1)) and binds RV warrantors only.

not_addressed.label: Audit basis (reasonable / non-retaliatory / not tied to a rate request)
not_addressed.note: No general requirement. The only anti-retaliation rule is § 23-112-319(c), limited to reductions made because a dealer filed a § 319 recall-reimbursement claim (recorded as a rule). § 403(a)(2)(U)(iii) bars unreasonable discrimination among franchisees in assistance programs 'including ... warranty policy adjustments', which is not an audit rule.

not_addressed.label: Recovery scope (whole claim vs. unsupported portion)
not_addressed.note: 'Charge back any false or unsubstantiated claims' does not say whether the whole claim or only the unsupported amount may be recovered. Do not infer whole-claim recovery.

not_addressed.label: Limits on claim documentation
not_addressed.note: The manufacturer may 'Require documentation for claims' with no stated limit. The 45-day additional-documentation cap in § 310(d)(1)(D)(iii) is a rate-submission rule, not a claim rule.

not_addressed.label: Dealer rebuttal period before a chargeback
not_addressed.note: No pre-chargeback rebuttal period. The dealer's response is the 90-day Commission appeal (recorded under chargeback_hold and stay_pending_dispute).

not_addressed.label: Written reasons for a chargeback
not_addressed.note: Only 'notification by the manufacturer or distributor' is mentioned, as the start of the 90-day appeal clock. The written-specific-grounds requirement applies to disapprovals of submitted claims.

legal_review.title: Fraud chargebacks outside the one-year window
legal_review.summary: § 23-112-313(e)(4)(C) allows a fraud chargeback on a court finding 'within a period not to exceed two (2) years from the date of the claim' without saying whether the two years bounds the finding or the chargeback, and names only 'the manufacturer' where the audit right names 'the manufacturer or franchiser'.
legal_review.text: § 23-112-313(e)(4)(C) lets 'the manufacturer' charge back a fraudulent claim if it establishes fraud in an Arkansas court of competent jurisdiction 'within a period not to exceed two (2) years from the date of the claim'. The sentence does not say whether the two-year limit governs the court finding or the chargeback, and it names only 'the manufacturer' while (e)(4)(A) grants the audit and chargeback rights to 'the manufacturer or franchiser' and (D) speaks of 'the manufacturer or distributor'. The statute does not reconcile the two-year attachment or the actor mismatch.
legal_review.action: Obtain legal interpretation before relying on (e)(4)(C), especially as a distributor-franchiser; until then, obtain the court finding and take the chargeback within two years of the claim date.

quotes.quote: charge back any fraudulent claim if the manufacturer establishes in a court of competent jurisdiction in this state that the claim is fraudulent within a period not to exceed two (2) years from the date of the claim

legal_review.title: Timing of the chargeback levy
legal_review.summary: The one-year period is written as the audit period and no deadline is stated for levying the chargeback; the statute also does not say whether a levy made inside the dealer's 90-day appeal window must be reversed if an appeal is then filed.
legal_review.text: § 23-112-313(e)(4)(A)(ii) lets the manufacturer or franchiser 'Audit the claims within a one-year period from the date the claim was paid or credit issued', and (iii) lets it 'Charge back any false or unsubstantiated claims' with no deadline. (e)(4)(D)(i) gives the dealer 90 days from notification to appeal to the Commission and (D)(ii) bars levying the chargeback once an appeal is filed. The statute does not say whether a chargeback from a timely audit may be notified or levied after the year ends, nor whether a chargeback levied before an appeal is filed must be reversed on filing.
legal_review.action: Obtain legal interpretation before levying a chargeback after the one-year (or 12-month incentive) period or inside the 90-day appeal window; until then, notify within the window and hold the levy until the appeal window closes or the appeal is resolved.

quotes.quote: Audit the claims within a one-year period from the date the claim was paid or credit issued by the manufacturer or franchiser
If a dealer files an appeal of the chargeback with the commission, the manufacturer or distributor shall not levy the chargeback until the appeal is resolved.

legal_review.title: Clerical errors on paid claims
legal_review.summary: § 23-112-313(e)(3)(A) bars disapproving a claim for a clerical error that does not change the amount, but the chargeback ground in (e)(4)(A)(iii) ('false or unsubstantiated') does not cross-reference it, so whether such a paid claim can be charged back is open.
legal_review.text: § 23-112-313(e)(3)(A) bars DISAPPROVAL of a claim for a clerical error that does not render the amount incorrect, including errors from the manufacturer's or distributor's prior-approval process. § 23-112-313(e)(4)(A)(iii) permits charging back 'any false or unsubstantiated claims' and does not cross-reference (e)(3)(A). The statute does not say whether a paid claim carrying such a clerical error can be treated as 'unsubstantiated' and charged back.
legal_review.action: Obtain legal interpretation before charging back a paid claim for a clerical or prior-approval error that does not change the claim amount.

quotes.quote: A claim shall not be disapproved because a clerical error was made that does not render the amount of the claim incorrect
Charge back any false or unsubstantiated claims.

penalties_line: An improper audit or chargeback exposes the manufacturer or distributor to a dealer's action for reasonable damages and attorney's fees for a willful failure to comply (§ 23-112-105(a)-(b)), and to Commission denial, suspension or revocation of its license for unfairly failing to fulfill a warranty agreement or fairly compensate dealers (§ 23-112-308(a)(18)(A)), or a penalty in lieu of up to $10,000 (revocation) or $50-$500 per day capped at $5,000 (suspension), each instance a separate violation (§ 23-112-309).

protest_forum.value: Appeal to the Arkansas Motor Vehicle Commission within 90 days of notification of the chargeback; the chargeback may not be levied while the appeal is pending; hearing within 120 days of filing unless all parties agree to settle; procedure under § 23-112-501 et seq., with further appeal under the Arkansas Administrative Procedure Act

notes: 1) Official code: the LexisNexis-hosted Arkansas Code on arkleg.state.ar.us was not read; the current text comes from the Justia 2025 edition (mirror) cross-checked against the enrolled acts (official) for every amendment since 2009 and the Commission-hosted 2011 Official Edition. Justia pages carry no 'current through' line; their histories for §§ 310, 313 and 319 end at 2021, 2023 and 2019 respectively. 2) Justia path: § 23-112-313 sits under title-23/subtitle-4 (Miscellaneous Regulated Industries); the subtitle-2 URL in the task brief returns 403 to curl and a client error to WebFetch. 3) 2025 session: no act amended §§ 310, 313 or 319. Acts 233 and 816 of 2025 (the only AMVC acts) amend § 302(e) and § 308(a)(25) (buyer's tags). The arkleg keyword search endpoint returned HTTP 500, so the session check rests on the Justia 2025 histories plus the two enrolled acts; the 2026 fiscal session was not checked. No pending bill found. 4) Act 924 of 2019 § 2 rewrote § 310(d)(3); pdftotext drops strike-through, but the Justia 2025 text ('shall pay ... in accordance with requirements of the manufacturer', no (A)-(D) subdivisions, no 'service technician' language anywhere in § 310) shows the act struck the 'safety and repair specifications, bulletins' words and the technician-preapproval subdivisions. 5) § 23-112-105(b): Act 1043 of 2013 § 3 added a (b)(2) excluding motor-home dealers, manufacturers and distributors from the fee action; the Justia 2024 extract showed (b) as one paragraph and the 2025 page was checked only for (a) — immaterial to a line-make auto manufacturer, but the (b)(2) carve-out was not confirmed in the 2025 text. 6) Drafting defect: codified (e)(1) says claims shall be approved or disapproved 'within thirty (30) days following their approval or disapproval' (so since Act 756 of 2009); the operative clocks are (e)(2)(B) and § 310(d)(2)(B). 7) Actor terms: (e)(4)(A)-(B) say 'manufacturer or franchiser', (C) 'the manufacturer', (D) 'manufacturer or distributor'. 'Franchiser' is not separately defined; § 103(14) uses it for 'a manufacturer or a distributor, importer, second-stage manufacturer, or converter as franchiser'. 8) Separate RV regime: § 23-112-1016 (Act 1043 of 2013) governs recreational-vehicle warrantors (audits 'on a reasonable basis', denial only for cause, 60-day payment); it does not apply to motor vehicle manufacturers under subchapter 3. 9) § 403 contains no audit, chargeback or export language; (a)(2)(U)(iii) bars unreasonable discrimination in assistance programs 'including ... warranty policy adjustments'. 10) Agency rules: the context shows no rule note, so scope is statutes only.
